mainTopic: Separating men and women at the שמחת בית השואבה, the future הספד in זכריה, and a series of אגדות about the power and names of the יצר הרע.
overview: This amud opens with a פסוק in זכריה about a great הספד in the future, where men and women mourn separately. From it the חכמים build a קל וחומר: if men and women are separated even during mourning, when the יצר הרע is weak, they must surely be separated at the joyous שמחת בית השואבה. The גמרא then asks what that future הספד is for. One view says it is for משיח בן יוסף, who is killed. The other says it is for the יצר הרע, and רבי יהודה explains that the righteous and the wicked will both weep when it is slaughtered, each for a different reason. Next the גמרא gathers teachings about the יצר הרע. It starts thin like a spider's thread and becomes strong like wagon ropes, and it has seven names given by God and the נביאים. A ברייתא on a פסוק in יואל describes the damage it has done, and אביי adds that it attacks תלמידי חכמים most of all. A story about אביי leads to the famous rule כל הגדול מחבירו יצרו גדול הימנו. The amud ends as רבי יצחק begins to teach that a person's יצר grows strong against him every day, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse about separate mourning in the future
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in זכריה that describes a future הספד where families mourn separately and the women mourn apart from the men.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the land will mourn, each family on its own: the family of בית דוד on its own, and their women on their own."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source for separating men and women. This is a setup for the קל וחומר that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important word is לבד, "separately." The פסוק says the men of each family mourn on their own and their women mourn on their own. This shows that even in the future, at a time of mourning, men and women are kept apart.

phrases.english: "And the land will mourn
family by family, separately;
the family of the house of David separately,
and their women separately."
phrases.notes: This is the key phrase: women mourn apart from men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of the תיקון גדול that separated men and women at the שמחת בית השואבה by supplying a scriptural source.
steps.raayaObject: That men and women should be separated at the שמחת בית השואבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 12:12, which describes men and women mourning separately in the future.

steps.title: All the more so during celebration
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים build a קל וחומר: if men and women are separated during mourning, when the יצר הרע is weak, they must surely be separated during celebration, when the יצר הרע is strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Isn't this a קל וחומר? If in the future, when people are busy mourning and the יצר הרע does not control them, the תורה still says men separately and women separately, then now, when people are busy celebrating and the יצר הרע does control them, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים use the פסוק to prove that men and women must be separated at the שמחת בית השואבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison rests on two differences. The future scene is mourning, which weakens the יצר הרע; the שמחת בית השואבה is celebration, which strengthens it. If separation is needed even in the easier case, it is certainly needed in the harder one.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
in the future to come (the days of משיח)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase אמרה תורה ("the תורה said") refers here to a פסוק in נביאים (זכריה). In this kind of usage, "תורה" means Scripture in general, not only the חומש.
steps.whatToRemember: Separating men and women at the שמחת בית השואבה is supported by a קל וחומר: mourning, when the יצר הרע is weak, still required separation, so celebration, when it is strong, surely does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the scriptural basis for the תיקון גדול of separate areas for men and women in the בית המקדש during the celebration.

phrases.english: They said: Are these matters not a kal vachomer?
If in the future to come,
when they are busy with mourning
and the evil inclination does not rule over them —
the Torah said
men separately and women separately.
Now, when they are busy with celebration
phrases.notes: Refers to the שמחת בית השואבה.

phrases.english: and the evil inclination does rule over them —
how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק from step 1 as the base case of a קל וחומר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Men and women must certainly be separated at the joyous שמחת בית השואבה.

steps.title: What is the future mourning for?
steps.stepSummary: Following up on the פסוק, the גמרא asks who or what the future הספד is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: This mourning, what is it about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side question raised by the פסוק: what will people be mourning in the future? This sets up the מחלוקת in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof about separation is already finished. The גמרא now asks about the content of the פסוק itself, because a great mourning in the days of the גאולה is surprising.

keyTerms.meaning: what is its nature / what is it about

phrases.english: This mourning, what is it about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Branches off from the פסוק quoted in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the future הספד described in זכריה.

steps.title: Two views: משיח בן יוסף or the יצר הרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא and the רבנן disagree. One says the mourning is for משיח בן יוסף, who is killed; the other says it is for the יצר הרע, which is killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא and the רבנן disagree about this. One says it is for משיח בן יוסף, who was killed. The other says it is for the יצר הרע, which was killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a מחלוקת between two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that someone or something is killed in the future, but they disagree about what. One view is a real tragedy, the death of משיח בן יוסף. The other is surprising, the death of the יצר הרע. The גמרא does not say which opinion belongs to רבי דוסא and which to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: the משיח from the tribe of יוסף, who is killed in war before משיח בן דוד

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa and the Rabbis disagree about it.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: עַל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג,
phrases.english: One said: It is for Messiah ben Yosef, who was killed,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: עַל יֵצֶר הָרַע שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג.
phrases.english: and one said: It is for the evil inclination, which was killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מחלוקת: the mourning is either for משיח בן יוסף or for the יצר הרע.

steps.title: Why cry when the יצר הרע dies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a nearby פסוק fits the משיח בן יוסף view, then challenges the יצר הרע view: the death of the יצר הרע should cause joy, not crying.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says the mourning is for משיח בן יוסף, who was killed. That is what is written: "They will look to Me because of the one they stabbed, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child." But according to the one who says it is for the יצר הרע, which was killed, is this a reason to mourn? It is a reason to celebrate! Why did they cry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the first view fits a nearby פסוק well, then challenges the second view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the משיח בן יוסף view, the פסוק about a person who was "stabbed" fits well, since a person was killed. For the יצר הרע view, the reaction seems backwards: losing the יצר הרע is good news. So why would anyone cry?

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense (according to one view)

steps.confusionAlert: The בשלמא part is not the challenge. It only says the first view works well. The real attack begins at אלא, against the יצר הרע view.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said
it is for Messiah ben Yosef, who was killed,
that is what is written:
"And they shall look to Me because of the one they stabbed,
and they shall mourn for him as one mourns for an only child."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַל יֵצֶר הָרַע שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג —
phrases.english: But according to the one who said it is for the evil inclination, which was killed —
is this a reason to make mourning?
One should make a celebration!
Why did they cry?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views from step 4 against the פסוק and against common sense.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the future mourning is for the יצר הרע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The death of the יצר הרע is good news, so it should bring celebration, not crying.

steps.title: Righteous and wicked both weep at the יצר הרע's slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי יהודה's דרשה, the גמרא explains that when הקדוש ברוך הוא slaughters the יצר הרע, the righteous and the wicked will both weep, each for a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהודה taught: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring the יצר הרע and slaughter it in front of the righteous and the wicked. To the righteous it will look like a tall mountain, and to the wicked it will look like a thin hair. Both groups will cry. The righteous will cry and say: "How were we able to conquer such a tall mountain!" The wicked will cry and say: "How were we not able to conquer this thin hair!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the crying is not grief over the יצר הרע itself, but a reaction to seeing it clearly at last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The righteous struggled hard against the יצר הרע, so it looks huge to them, and they cry in amazement that they overcame it. The wicked gave in easily, so it looks tiny to them, and they cry in regret that they did not resist something so small. Either way the crying is explained without saying anyone is sad the יצר הרע is gone.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehuda expounded:

phrases.aramaic: לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, מְבִיאוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיֵצֶר הָרָע,
phrases.english: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bring the evil inclination
and slaughter it in front of the righteous and in front of the wicked.
To the righteous it appears like a tall mountain,
and to the wicked it appears like a strand of hair.
These cry and those cry.
The righteous cry and say:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ יָכוֹלְנוּ לִכְבּוֹשׁ הַר גָּבוֹהַּ כָּזֶה!
phrases.english: How were we able to conquer such a tall mountain!
And the wicked cry and say:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ לֹא יָכוֹלְנוּ לִכְבּוֹשׁ אֶת חוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה הַזֶּה!
phrases.english: How were we unable to conquer this strand of hair!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reason for the crying.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Crying must mean people are grieving the loss of the יצר הרע, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The crying comes from amazement (the righteous) and regret (the wicked) when they see the יצר הרע clearly at last.
steps.whyThisMatters: The image teaches that a person who fights the יצר הרע experiences it as huge, while a person who gives in comes to see it as weak and small.

steps.title: Even הקדוש ברוך הוא wonders with them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה ends by saying that הקדוש ברוך הוא will also wonder along with them, and brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even הקדוש ברוך הוא will wonder along with them, as it says: "So says ה׳ of hosts: If it will be wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, it will also be wondrous in My eyes."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה completes his דרשה with a פסוק showing that the amazement is shared by הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word יפלא, "wondrous," for both the people and ה׳. This supports the idea that the future scene is one of deep amazement, which is why there is weeping, and not simple sadness. It strengthens the answer to why people cry when the יצר הרע is killed.
steps.whatToRemember: The future mourning is either for משיח בן יוסף or for the יצר הרע. According to the second view, the crying comes from amazement and regret when everyone sees how big or how small the יצר הרע really was, and even הקדוש ברוך הוא shares in the wonder.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא תָּמֵהַּ עִמָּהֶם,
phrases.english: And even the Holy One, Blessed be He, wonders with them,
as it is said: "So says the Lord of hosts:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי יִפָּלֵא בְּעֵינֵי שְׁאֵרִית הָעָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: If it will be wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people
in those days, it will also be wondrous in My eyes."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא תָּמֵהַּ עִמָּהֶם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהודה's דרשה from step 6 with a scriptural source.
steps.raayaObject: That the future scene is one of wonder, shared even by הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: The evil inclination starts thin and grows strong
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי teaches that the יצר הרע begins as weak as a spider's thread but ends up as strong as wagon ropes, and he brings a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: At first the יצר הרע is like a spider's thread, but in the end it is like the thick ropes of a wagon, as the פסוק says: 'Woe to those who pull sin with cords of emptiness, and sin as if with wagon ropes.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the previous steps were about the יצר הרע, the גמרא now adds another teaching about it. רב אסי describes how it grows over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions two kinds of ropes: thin 'cords of emptiness' and thick 'wagon ropes.' רב אסי reads these as two stages of the same יצר הרע. It starts weak and easy to break, but if a person keeps giving in, it becomes a strong rope that drags him.

keyTerms.meaning: The evil inclination, the inner drive to sin
A strand of a spider's web, a very thin thread
Thick ropes used to tie or pull a wagon
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical lesson: it is easiest to fight the יצר הרע at the very beginning, before it grows strong.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
The evil inclination, at first,
is like a strand of a spider's web,
and in the end it is like the ropes of a wagon,
as it says: 'Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity,'
'and sin as with a wagon rope.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related אגדה about the יצר הרע after the discussion of its future slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע starts weak like a thin thread and becomes strong like wagon ropes.

steps.title: God invites משיח בן דוד to ask for anything
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא will tell משיח בן דוד to ask for whatever he wants, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: To משיח בן דוד, who will be revealed soon in our days, הקדוש ברוך הוא says: Ask Me for something and I will give it to you, as the פסוק says: 'I will tell of the decree... today I have given birth to you. Ask of Me and I will give nations as your inheritance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about משיח בן דוד. This line sets up the story that comes next, where we find out what he actually asks for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים ב shows God speaking to a chosen king and saying 'ask of Me.' The ברייתא reads this as an open offer to משיח בן דוד. This links back to step 4, where we learned that משיח בן יוסף will be killed.

keyTerms.meaning: The final redeemer, a descendant of דוד המלך

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Mashiach ben David, who is destined to be revealed
swiftly in our days,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, says to him:
Ask Me for something and I will give it to you,
as it says: 'I will tell of the decree, etc.'
'This day I have begotten you.'
'Ask of Me, and I will give nations as your inheritance.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of the two משיחים from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא offers משיח בן דוד anything he asks for.

steps.title: משיח בן דוד asks only for life
steps.stepSummary: After seeing משיח בן יוסף killed, משיח בן דוד asks הקדוש ברוך הוא only for life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he sees that משיח בן יוסף was killed, he says before Him: רבונו של עולם! I ask You only for life.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. משיח בן דוד uses the open offer to ask for just one thing: that he should live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He could have asked for anything, even the nations of the world. But he has just seen משיח בן יוסף killed, so his only request is not to die the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: An earlier redeemer from the tribe of יוסף, who is killed in battle

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁרָאָה מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג,
phrases.english: And once he saw Mashiach ben Yosef, who was killed,
he says before Him: Master of the world!
I ask of You only life.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁרָאָה מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what משיח בן דוד does with the offer from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיח בן דוד asks only for life.

steps.title: God answers that דוד המלך already prophesied it
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא replies that דוד המלך already foretold this request and its answer, and brings a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says to him: Life? Even before you said it, your father דוד already prophesied about you, as the פסוק says: 'He asked You for life, You gave it to him...'
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers the request. He proves from a פסוק that life was already promised to משיח בן דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים כא speaks of a king who 'asked for life' and received it. The ברייתא reads this as דוד prophesying about his descendant, משיח בן דוד. The request is granted before it is even made.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked You for life (תהלים כא:ה)

steps.whatToRemember: משיח בן דוד will be promised life, unlike משיח בן יוסף who is killed. This was already foretold by דוד המלך in תהלים.

phrases.english: He says to him: Life?
Before you even said it,
your father David already prophesied about you,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לוֹ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'He asked life of You, You gave it to him, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request from step 10 and supports the answer with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That משיח בן דוד is promised life
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים כא:ה, ״חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לוֹ״

steps.title: The evil inclination has seven names, and God called it evil
steps.stepSummary: רבי עוירא (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) teaches that the יצר הרע has seven names. The first is 'רע,' the name God gave it, as shown by a פסוק in בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עוירא, and some say רבי יהושע בן לוי, taught: The יצר הרע has seven names. הקדוש ברוך הוא called it 'evil,' as the פסוק says: 'For the inclination of a man's heart is evil from his youth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of the יצר הרע with a new list: its seven names. This step gives the opening statement and the first name on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name comes from a different speaker in תנ״ך, and each is backed by a פסוק. God Himself calls it 'רע' in בראשית ח, after the flood.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another possible author of the teaching)

phrases.english: Rabbi Avira taught,
and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְעָה שֵׁמוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע.
phrases.english: The evil inclination has seven names.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, called it 'evil,'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעוּרָיו״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'For the inclination of a man's heart is evil from his youth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי עַוִּירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new list-teaching about the יצר הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע has seven names. The first is 'רע,' given by God.

steps.title: משה called it uncircumcised
steps.stepSummary: The second name: משה called the יצר הרע 'ערל,' based on the פסוק about circumcising the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה called it 'uncircumcised,' as the verse says: 'And you shall circumcise the foreskin of your hearts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with the second name, which comes from משה רבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the heart has a 'foreskin' that must be removed, then something is blocking the heart. That blocking layer is the יצר הרע, so משה calls it 'ערל.'

keyTerms.meaning: The foreskin of your hearts (דברים י:טז)

phrases.english: Moshe called it 'uncircumcised,'
as it says: 'And you shall circumcise the foreskin of your hearts.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the list of seven names.
steps.raayaObject: The name 'ערל' for the יצר הרע

steps.title: דוד called it impure
steps.stepSummary: The third name: דוד המלך called the יצר הרע 'טמא.' This is learned by inference from his request for a pure heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד called it 'impure,' as the פסוק says: 'Create for me a pure heart, O God.' By implication, there is an impure one.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with the third name, from דוד המלך. Here the name is not written openly in the פסוק, so the גמרא learns it by inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'a pure heart.' The גמרא reasons that if דוד had to ask for a pure heart, then there must also be an impure heart. That impure heart is the יצר הרע.

phrases.english: David called it 'impure,'
as it says: 'Create for me a pure heart, O God,'
which implies that there is an impure one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the list. Unlike the earlier names, it is proven by inference.
steps.raayaObject: The name 'טמא' for the יצר הרע

steps.title: שלמה called it enemy
steps.stepSummary: The fourth name: שלמה המלך called the יצר הרע 'שונא,' based on a פסוק in משלי about feeding a hungry enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה called it 'enemy,' as the פסוק says: 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink. For you are heaping coals on his head, and ה׳ will reward you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with the fourth name, from שלמה המלך. This step quotes the פסוק, and the next step explains how to read its last words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'enemy' in this פסוק is read as the יצר הרע. The גמרא does not explain the 'bread' and 'water' here. Its point is the name 'שונא', and in the next step it rereads the פסוק's last words.

phrases.english: Shlomo called it 'enemy,'
as it says: 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread,'
'and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink,'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי גֶחָלִים אַתָּה חוֹתֶה עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
phrases.english: 'for you are heaping coals upon his head,'
'and ה׳ will reward you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth item in the list of names.
steps.raayaObject: The name 'שונא' for the יצר הרע

steps.title: God will make peace between you and the evil inclination
steps.stepSummary: Using an אל תקרי reading, the גמרא rereads 'ישלם לך' (will reward you) as 'ישלימנו לך' (will make it at peace with you).
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not read it as 'He will reward you,' but rather as 'He will make it at peace with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last words of שלמה's פסוק in a new way. The point is that God will turn the יצר הרע from an enemy into a friend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of 'ישלם' can also be read as related to 'שלום,' peace. So the reward for fighting the 'enemy' is that God makes the יצר הרע stop fighting you.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as (a rereading of a word in a פסוק for a lesson)
He will make it at peace with you

steps.confusionAlert: An אל תקרי does not mean the written פסוק is wrong or changed. It adds an extra layer of meaning on top of the simple reading.

phrases.english: Do not read 'He will reward you,'
but rather 'He will make it at peace with you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets the end of the פסוק quoted in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who fights the יצר הרע properly will be rewarded by God making the יצר הרע at peace with him.

steps.title: Fifth name: ישעיה calls it a stumbling block
steps.stepSummary: ישעיה called the יצר הרע 'מכשול,' a stumbling block, based on a פסוק about clearing the way for God's people.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיה called it 'stumbling block,' as it says: 'Pave, pave, clear the road, remove the stumbling block from the road of My people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of names for the יצר הרע and gives the fifth one, 'מכשול,' with a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about removing an obstacle from the path of the Jewish people. The גמרא reads that obstacle as the יצר הרע, which trips a person up on his way to serving God.

keyTerms.meaning: A stumbling block, an obstacle that trips you

phrases.english: Isaiah called it 'stumbling block,' as it says:
'Pave, pave, clear the road,
remove the stumbling block from the road of My people.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of seven names after שלמה's name 'שונא' (steps 15-16).
steps.raayaObject: The name 'מכשול' for the יצר הרע

steps.title: Sixth name: יחזקאל calls it stone
steps.stepSummary: יחזקאל called the יצר הרע 'אבן,' a stone, from the פסוק promising to replace the heart of stone with a heart of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: יחזקאל called it 'stone,' as it says: 'I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the sixth name, 'אבן,' and proves it from a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'heart of stone' is a hard heart that does not respond to good. The יצר הרע makes the heart hard like this, so יחזקאל calls it 'stone.'

keyTerms.meaning: A heart of stone: a hard, unfeeling heart
A heart of flesh: a soft, responsive heart

phrases.english: Ezekiel called it 'stone,' as it says:
'And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh,
and I will give you a heart of flesh.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next name in the same list.
steps.raayaObject: The name 'אבן' for the יצר הרע

steps.title: Seventh name: יואל calls it the hidden one
steps.stepSummary: יואל called the יצר הרע 'צפוני,' from the פסוק 'I will remove the צפוני far from you.' This completes the list of seven names.
steps.simpleTranslation: יואל called it 'the hidden one,' as it says: 'And the צפוני I will remove far from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the seventh and final name, 'צפוני,' with a פסוק from יואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of 'צפוני' is 'the northern one,' meaning an enemy from the north. The גמרא reads it as the יצר הרע. The next step explains why this name fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'northern one'; here read as 'hidden one' (from צָפוּן)
I will distance / remove far away

steps.whatToRemember: The seven names are: רע (God), ערל (משה), טמא (דוד), שונא (שלמה), מכשול (ישעיה), אבן (יחזקאל), צפוני (יואל).

phrases.english: Joel called it 'the hidden/northern one,' as it says:
'And the northern one I will remove far from you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final name, which completes the list of seven.
steps.raayaObject: The name 'צפוני' for the יצר הרע

steps.title: A teaching explains why it is called the hidden one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that the צפוני in יואל's פסוק is the יצר הרע, because it is hidden away in a person's heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And the צפוני I will remove far from you.' This is the יצר הרע, which is hidden and stays in a person's heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the name 'צפוני.' This opens a longer explanation of the whole פסוק in יואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא connects צפוני to the word צָפוּן, meaning hidden. The יצר הרע sits quietly inside a person's heart, so we often do not notice it working.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught: introduces a ברייתא
The evil inclination, a person's drive toward sin

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'צפוני' here means a real army from the north. That is the simple reading of the פסוק, but the ברייתא reads it as the hidden יצר הרע.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And the northern one I will remove far from you':
this is the evil inclination,
which is hidden and stays in a person's heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the last name (צפוני) by bringing a ברייתא that reads the whole פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צפוני means the יצר הרע, because it hides in a person's heart.

steps.title: God will banish it to a place with no people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: 'a barren and desolate land' means a place with no people for the יצר הרע to provoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And I will drive it to a barren and desolate land': to a place where there are no people around for it to provoke.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps explaining יואל's פסוק, now the part about where God will send the יצר הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment fits the יצר הרע's job. Its whole purpose is to provoke people, so God will put it somewhere with no people at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will drive it away
To provoke, to pick a fight with

phrases.english: 'And I will drive it to a barren and desolate land':
to a place where people are not found
for it to provoke them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase of the same פסוק, explained by the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, the יצר הרע will be exiled to a place with no one to tempt.

steps.title: It destroyed both Temples and killed the scholars in them
steps.stepSummary: The 'eastern (קדמוני) sea' refers to the first מקדש and the 'last (אחרון) sea' refers to the second מקדש. The יצר הרע set its eyes on each one, destroyed it, and killed its תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Its face toward the eastern sea': it set its eyes on the first מקדש, destroyed it, and killed the תלמידי חכמים in it. 'And its end toward the last sea': it set its eyes on the second מקדש, destroyed it, and killed the תלמידי חכמים in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the next two phrases of the פסוק. It says they describe the damage the יצר הרע has already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses wordplay. קדמוני ('eastern') sounds like 'first,' and אחרון ('western/last') means 'last.' It reads them as the first and second בית המקדש, which were destroyed because of sins that the יצר הרע brought about.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern sea; read as 'the first'

phrases.english: 'Its face toward the eastern sea':
for it set its eyes on the First Temple and destroyed it,
and killed the Torah scholars in it.
'And its end toward the western (last) sea':
for it set its eyes on the Second Temple and destroyed it,
and killed the Torah scholars in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא on the next phrases of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע is responsible for the destruction of both בתי המקדש and the death of their scholars.

steps.title: It leaves the nations alone and targets the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: 'Its stench will rise' means the יצר הרע leaves the other nations alone and focuses on provoking ישראל. The text uses a polite way of speaking and says 'the enemies of ישראל' when it means ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Its stench will rise and its foul smell will rise': because it leaves the nations of the world alone and provokes the enemies of ישראל (a polite way of saying ישראל itself).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains another phrase of the פסוק. It says the יצר הרע's 'stench' is that it saves its strongest attacks for the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'enemies of ישראל' are a respectful substitute. The ברייתא does not want to say something bad directly about ישראל. The point is that the יצר הרע works hardest against the people closest to God.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Enemies of ישראל': a polite way of saying ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: 'שונאיהם של ישראל' does not mean real enemies of the Jews. It is a polite way of saying ישראל itself, so the text does not speak negatively about them.

phrases.english: 'Its stench will rise and its foul smell will rise':
for it leaves the nations of the world alone,
and provokes the 'enemies' of Israel (a euphemism for Israel).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase of the same פסוק in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע attacks ישראל more than the other nations.

steps.title: אביי: it attacks Torah scholars most of all
steps.stepSummary: On the last phrase, 'for it has done greatly,' אביי says the יצר הרע attacks תלמידי חכמים more than anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For it has done greatly': אביי said, and it attacks תלמידי חכמים more than all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds his own explanation of the last phrase of the פסוק. He takes the idea one step further: among ישראל, scholars are targeted the most.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said the יצר הרע targets ישראל more than the nations. אביי narrows it further to תלמידי חכמים. The more spiritual a person is, the harder the יצר הרע works against him.

phrases.english: 'For it has done greatly':
Abaye said:
And against Torah scholars more than all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 23 and narrows the target from ישראל to תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע attacks תלמידי חכמים more than anyone else.

steps.title: אביי follows a man and woman to prevent sin
steps.stepSummary: אביי heard a man and woman plan to travel together early in the morning. He followed them for three פרסאות through the marshes to stop them from sinning. When they parted, nothing had happened, and they simply said it had been a pleasant trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this story: אביי heard a certain man say to a certain woman, 'Let us get up early and go on the road.' He said, 'I will go and keep them away from sin.' He followed them for three פרסאות through the marshes. When they separated from each other, he heard them saying, 'The road was long, and the company was pleasant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to illustrate אביי's statement that the יצר הרע attacks scholars more than others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the two would sin, but they behaved properly the whole way. This sets up the lesson in the next step: these ordinary people held back easily, and אביי realized his own struggle would have been harder.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us get up early and go

phrases.english: Like this: Abaye heard
a certain man saying to a certain woman:
'Let us get up early and go on the road.'
He said: 'I will go and keep them away from sin.'
He went after them three parasangs through the marsh.
When they were separating from each other,
he heard them saying:
'Our road is long, and our company is pleasant.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that illustrates אביי's statement in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the יצר הרע attacks תלמידי חכמים most
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man and woman on the road

steps.title: אביי realizes he could not have held back, and is distressed
steps.stepSummary: אביי said that if it had been himself in that situation, he could not have controlled himself. He leaned against the doorpost in distress.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'If it had been the one who hates me (meaning myself), he would not have been able to control himself.' He went and leaned against the door's archway, feeling distressed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a painful lesson from the story: his own יצר הרע is stronger than that ordinary man's. He feels upset about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The one who hates me' is a polite way of saying 'me.' This shows the point of step 24 in a real person: the great scholar has the stronger temptation. His sadness sets up the old man's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One who hates me': a polite way of saying 'myself'
The doorpost or archway of a door

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not talking about an enemy. 'מאן דסני לי' is a polite way of referring to himself.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If it had been 'the one who hates me' (i.e., me),
he would not have been able to restrain himself.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל תְּלָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּעִיבּוּרָא דְּדָשָׁא וּמִצְטַעֵר.
phrases.english: He went and leaned against the doorpost and was distressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִי מַאן דְּסָנֵי לִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי's reaction to the outcome of the story.
steps.raayaObject: That a scholar's יצר הרע is stronger than an ordinary person's

steps.title: An elder: the greater the person, the greater his evil inclination
steps.stepSummary: An old man came and taught אביי that whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater יצר הרע. His strong temptation is a sign of his greatness, so it is not a reason to despair.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain old man came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his יצר הרע is greater than his fellow's.
steps.whatsHappening: An elder comforts אביי with a principle that sums up the whole section: great people face great temptations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's strong temptation does not show that he is worse than the simple man. It shows that he is greater. This confirms אביי's own statement in step 24 that the יצר הרע targets תלמידי חכמים most.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever is greater than his fellow

steps.whatToRemember: כל הגדול מחבירו יצרו גדול הימנו: whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater יצר הרע. A strong יצר הרע is a sign of spiritual stature, not of failure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous principle in מוסר. It teaches that a person struggling with strong temptation should not despair, because the struggle comes with his greatness.

phrases.english: A certain elder came and taught him:
Whoever is greater than his fellow,
his inclination is greater than his (fellow's).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's distress and states the general principle behind the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The greater a person is, the stronger his יצר הרע. This is why תלמידי חכמים are targeted most.

steps.title: A person's inclination overpowers him every day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a person's יצר הרע grows strong against him each day, and starts to bring a פסוק as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day, as it says in the פסוק: 'Only...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי יצחק: the יצר הרע fights a person every single day. He starts quoting a פסוק to prove it, and the rest of the פסוק comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps said the יצר is stronger against greater people. Now רבי יצחק adds a point about time: the battle is not a one-time event but happens every day. The word 'רק' opens the proof-verse, which continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: His inclination (here, the evil inclination, יצר הרע)
As it is said, introduces a פסוק as a source
Only, the first word of the proof-verse

steps.confusionAlert: The text stops at 'רק' in the middle of the פסוק. Don't look for the proof here. The rest of the פסוק and the explanation come on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A person's inclination
overpowers him every day,
as it is stated: "Only
phrases.notes: The beginning of the proof-verse, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the theme of the יצר הרע's strength from Step 27, adding that the battle happens every day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's יצר הרע grows strong against him every day. This is supported by a פסוק that begins with 'רק'.
